references.text: The first fruits of your land's harvest you shall bring to the house of the Lord, your God. This is a parallel command to bring the first fruits to the Lord.
The best of your land's first fruits you shall bring to the house of the Lord, your God. Repeats the commandment regarding the first fruits.
Concerns offerings when Israel enters the land, including the first fruits of the dough as a gift to the Lord.
Describes the ceremony for bringing the first fruits when Israel enters the promised land, with a confession of God's faithfulness.
Israel celebrated Passover in Gilgal and ate from the produce of the land, marking the fulfillment of the promise to enter the land.
Mentions the first fruits of grain as part of the people's gifts to the priests and Levites.
Christ has been raised as the first fruits of those who have fallen asleep. The sheaf (omer) that was waved on the day after the Sabbath points prophetically forward to Christ's resurrection.
The believers are a first fruits of God's creatures, born again by the word of truth.
The 144,000 were purchased from among mankind as a first fruits for God and the Lamb.
